title: Dynamic Grid Trading Strategy: From Zero Expectation to Market Outperformance

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper introduces the Dynamic Grid-based Trading (DGT) strategy for cryptocurrencies, which continuously resets geometric grid levels and reinvests arbitrage profits when prices exceed predefined upper or lower boundaries, rather than terminating. Using 1-minute high-frequency spot candlestick data from Binance, the strategy is backtested across various parameter combinations of grid size and grid number counts.
extraction.universe: Binance spot cryptocurrency markets (specifically Bitcoin and Ethereum)

key_findings: Traditional grid trading strategies without market trend insight have an expected value of zero before transaction fees, resulting in losses once fees are included.
The proposed Dynamic Grid-based Trading (DGT) strategy achieves consistently positive annualized returns (60-70%) by continuously resetting grids and avoiding premature termination.
The DGT strategy outperforms the traditional buy-and-hold strategy by achieving higher returns with significantly lower maximum drawdowns on BTC and better risk control on ETH.
Smaller grid sizes suffer heavily from transaction fee proportions, while large grid sizes and grid numbers result in infrequent activations and poor IRR performance.
limitations: Backtests rely on historical data from a period with a significant cryptocurrency price rise, which is highly favorable for spot grid trading.
